comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose performance metrics for specific commercial segments within their broader market platforms. NVIDIA highlights growth in its Automotive segment, reporting $1.1 billion in revenue up 21%, driven by partnerships with OEMs like MediaTek and Foxconn. In contrast, AMD reports a significant decline in its Gaming segment, with net revenue falling 58% to $2.6 billion due to lower semi-custom product revenue. While both operate in the semiconductor market and report segment-specific financial outcomes, NVIDIA's disclosed driver was growth in automotive AI platforms, whereas AMD's was a contraction in gaming hardware sales.

sentences.text: Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $1.1 billion, up 21% from fiscal year 2023.
In Automotive, we announced a partnership with MediaTek, which will develop mainstream automotive systems on chips for global OEMs integrating a new NVIDIA GPU chiplet IP for AI and graphics.
Gaming net revenue of $2.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 58%, compared to net revenue of $6.2 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue.
